name: Spoons (Pig)
description: Spoons (Pig) is the token-grabbing version of Pig: players pass cards to collect four of a kind, then the first successful player takes a spoon and everyone else races to take one of the remaining spoons.

content.text: Spoons (Pig) is the token-grabbing version of Pig: players pass cards to collect four of a kind, then the first successful player takes a spoon and everyone else races to take one of the remaining spoons.

A family of simple card-passing games played in a circle; players pass one card left and try to collect four of a kind. The group has no single documented inventor. Pig uses a nose-touch signal; Spoons uses one fewer spoon than players in the center. Regional variants include Bouchon (France, with corks), Donkey (Australia, sometimes called Hog), Vatra and Magarac (Bosnia and Herzegovina), and Popa Prostul (Romania). More dangerous variants use forks or knives instead of spoons. Widely played as a parlor and children's game, with many contributors to the documented rules.
2 to 13 (up to 13 with one 52-card pack; more with multiple packs).
Standard 52-card pack, or multiple packs for more than 12 players.
One spoon fewer than the number of players, placed in the center where any player can reach.
Four cards dealt to each player clockwise. Remainder forms the stock to dealer's right (stock version), or use four cards of one rank per player with no stock.

items.text: With stock pile: Full 52-card deck; four cards each, remainder forms stock to dealer's right. Dealer draws from stock; player to dealer's right discards to a discard pile. When stock is exhausted, shuffle discard to form new stock.

Without stock pile: Use four cards of one rank per player (e.g. 16 cards for 4 players: aces, kings, queens, jacks). No stock; all players pass one card left simultaneously. First to collect four of a kind takes a spoon.
